questions.explanation: Decisions made at the moment of speaking use 'will'.
questions.q: A: The phone is ringing. B: I ___ answer it.

questions.explanation: After 'will' always use the base verb.
options: I will to call you later.

questions.explanation: 'Won't' expresses refusal: she refuses to help.
questions.q: She says she ___ help us tomorrow.
It ___ rain tomorrow, so take an umbrella.

questions.explanation: Agreeing to do something now uses 'will'.
questions.q: A: Can you open the door? B: Sure, I ___.

Don't lend him money. He ___ pay you back.
We ___ you at the airport. Don't worry.
A: I don't understand. B: I ___ explain again.

questions.explanation: After 'will' use the base verb: 'will come', not 'will to come'.
questions.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
I'm sure you ___ the exam.
A: Would you like some tea? B: Yes, I ___ have some.
I ___ forget your birthday. I promise.

questions.explanation: 'Won't' can show refusal, even for a baby.
questions.q: The baby ___ sleep. She's too excited.

questions.explanation: Offers decided at the moment use 'will'.
questions.q: A: It's heavy. B: I ___ carry it for you.
